 ## Readiness — the checklist behind `completed` and behind publishing
 
 `keryx review readiness <review-id-or-path> [--json]` reads the package and prints every readiness item, READY or NOT READY, each with the evidence and the command that repairs it. It writes nothing, and exits non-zero when the verdict is NOT READY. Only item 9 reaches GitHub (the PR's own file list); the TUI and `review status` read the package alone.
 
 1. `files-covered` — every changed file is in a wave or carries a recorded waiver.
 2. `blast-radius` — no file the blast radius cut is left unreviewed. A cut radius writes `chunks.json`; run `keryx review chunks plan`, `estimate`, `next`/`record`, `merge`. In an unattended run every wave runs without a question, up to the 25-pass ceiling; in an interactive run the operator is asked once: in keryx shell call `review_chunks_answer` (a card, never a terminal); elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review chunks estimate --package <dir> --answer yes --quote "<their words>"` in their terminal; unattended, record Not run.
 3. `reviewers` — every planned reviewer was dispatched and its result ingested.
 4. `verifier` — the verifier checked every finding it should, or the report says how many it did not.
 5. `ledger` — the ledger is READY.
 6. `coverage-md` — coverage.md does not list a reviewer as `run` that the dispatch record says did not finish. Re-run `keryx review ingest` for the package.
 7. `head` — the report's head is the PR head.
 8. `report-names` — pending mutation candidates and parity warnings are named in the report.
 9. `pr-files` — the changed-file count equals the PR's own file list. A recount more than 3x the recorded scope is refused: it came from the wrong base. Recount with `keryx review blast-radius --package <ref> --changed <the PR's files>`.
 10. `memory-outside-stage` — the orchestrator read memory only in its memory stage ("Clean context" above). Outside keryx shell it reads "not observable on this host" unless this session's keryx calls carry the caller token `keryx review start` printed.
 11. `premise-decisions` — every finding `review-premise` held (`challenged` or `owner-decision`) has an operator decision: in keryx shell the card `review_decide_premise`; elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review decide-premise --package <dir> --finding <global_id> --answer uphold|dismiss --reason "<why>"` in their terminal (SKILL.md "Wave D"). Not waivable: each held finding needs its own answer, and `review_waive_readiness` / `--waive` refuse this item.
 12. `quotes-located` — every open finding whose quote `review ingest` could not place (absent from the file at the reviewed head, or in it more than once) has a disposition. Ingest keeps such a finding with no line, flagged `quote_unlocated` and listed in scope.md, instead of refusing the round. Re-quote one distinct line and re-ingest, record a disposition, or the operator waives the item.
 
-`keryx review complete` refuses status `completed` while any item fails. A failing item other than `premise-decisions` is waived only by the operator. In keryx shell call `review_waive_readiness` for the item: the operator answers it as a card, the waiver is recorded with the card text and the time, and then you call the `review_complete` card (the operator answers it in the shell or in the Telegram topic) or run `keryx review complete`. Never send the operator to a terminal. Outside keryx shell the operator runs `keryx review complete --waive <item> "<their own words>"` in a terminal, repeatable. Unattended, record the item as Not run. `keryx review publish` is held by the same checklist. Publishing is the operator's decision too: in keryx shell call `review_publish` (a card shows the target and the body; never send the operator to a terminal). A not-ready package goes to GitHub only as a partial review (`review_publish` with `partial: true`, or `keryx review publish --partial`), which puts a "Partial review" header on the post and never approves. The shell guard stops a publish command that runs through the keryx shell; a publisher outside it (CI, another agent, a script file) is not stopped, and that limit is named, not hidden.

 ## Fix rounds — dispositions, regressions, withdrawal
 
 ### Every prior finding leaves the round with a disposition
 
 A fix round that reports only new findings is unreadable: the author cannot tell
 which of their fixes landed. Close the loop explicitly — one line per prior
 finding, in the report, before the new findings:
 
 | Disposition | Meaning |
 |---|---|
 | `closed` | Checked against the code, not against the commit message, and the defect is gone |
 | `open` | The fix does not reach the defect; say what is still true |
 | `partial` | One site of the class was fixed and the enumeration named others |
 | `regressed` | The fix removed this defect and introduced another — file the new one separately |
 | `withdrawn` | The finding was wrong. See below |
 
 **Check the code, not the commit message.** A commit titled *"report an abandoned
 sync as abandoned"* is a claim; the disposition is whether the branch it renamed
 is reachable and pinned. On a recorded round, two such commits asserted behaviour

## Slices, waves and results — every host; keryx shell specifics marked
 
 A reviewer starts in the project root and reads project files; a path outside the project root is unreadable to it. On keryx shell its `context_files` content reaches it wrapped as DATA, and slices and measurements travel only there (never pasted or retyped); elsewhere the prompt names the slice paths. `skill_path` and `pr_context` stay payload fields. The text reaches the reviewer in slices small enough to finish.
 
 0. **Publish the plan before anything else (keryx shell).** Your first tool call is `plan_set` with `step-0`…`step-14` and `step-10b` all `pending`. A shell turn that has open plan items is continued by the host; a turn that ends on a text reply is over, and a message saying the review "cannot be honestly completed" ends the run with nothing reviewed. Never end the turn while a step is `pending` or `in_progress`: mark it `blocked` only with a cause you cannot fix with a command, and otherwise keep working. Step 6a then updates this plan rather than creating it.
 1. **Slice first.** `keryx review slice --ref <base> --package <package> --host <host>` after `keryx review start`. It writes `<package>/slices/slice-NN.diff` files of at most 150000 bytes each and a `manifest.json` carrying a wave budget (`--wave-bytes`, never below the slice ceiling; default by `--host`: 60000 on keryx-shell, 150000 elsewhere): what ONE reviewer dispatch may total, so a role owning many slices is dispatched in slice waves that each fit the child deadline. On keryx shell with a large diff pass a small `--max-bytes` (for example 18000) and `--wave-bytes` (for example 54000) so no wave outruns a reviewer's five minutes; ledgers (csv, lockfiles, snapshots, generated files) are listed under `omissions` with a reason — list them in the report as not reviewed, never as clean.
 2. **Slices travel by path; on keryx shell, only by `context_files`.** The slices sit under the project (`<package>/slices`). On keryx shell pass each reviewer its slice paths in `spawn_subagent`'s `context_files`: the host copies the text into that reviewer's task, so you never paste or retype a slice. Elsewhere name the slice paths in the prompt. Put the `slices` ids in its reviewer-input. A dispatch that names a git range but no slice leaves the reviewer with nothing to read — that is `BLOCKED`, not a review.
 3. **Check before dispatch, every payload.** `keryx review dispatch-check --payload <file> --manifest <package>/slices/manifest.json --package <package>` for the wave; exit 1 means a payload names no slice, is over the wave ceiling (dispatch fewer slices, then the next wave), names a `skill_path` or `context_doc` that does not exist (`REVIEWER_INPUT_PATH_MISSING`), belongs to an unconfirmed over-threshold plan (`REVIEWER_INPUT_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED`), or breaks `reviewer-input.schema.json`. Fix it; do not dispatch around it.
 4. **One batch.** Dispatch the whole wave — up to 10 reviewers — in one message, not one at a time. On keryx shell every round reviewer's `spawn_subagent` carries `review_wave: {"package": "<package>", "pass": "round"}` (a wave outside it counts against the turn's 32 children) and a `timeout_ms` that fits its wave: the default 300000 is sized for a wave of 60000 bytes, so a larger `--wave-bytes` needs a larger `timeout_ms`. Give each reviewer `max_rounds` of at least 40 (the default); a reviewer that spends its rounds reading the skill and the schema returns nothing. **Incomplete means the next wave while it makes progress, Not run when it stalls.** Every reviewer result lists the `slices` it covered, in its `REVIEW_RESULT` object, as ids (`"slices": ["slice-01", "slice-02"]`); an object with an `id` and an optional `coverage` note (`{"id": "slice-01", "coverage": "read in full"}`) is read the same way. An object with a `status` counts only when it is DONE, COMPLETE, COVERED or OK (any case); a slice marked NOT_READ, INCOMPLETE, SKIPPED or PARTIAL is not covered, so give a slice you did not read no `status` of that kind and leave it out. An entry with no id counts for nothing. **One driver file per dispatch.** Write `<package>/drivers/<reviewer>.json` with `{"reviewer": "<name>", "slices": [<ids dispatched>], "result": "raw/<reviewer>.txt", "definition": "<path of the reviewer's SKILL.md>"}`: `ledger build` takes the reviewer's rule file from `definition` (a `skill_path` there, or inside a `payload` object, is read too) and the slices it was handed from `slices`. Only reviewer replies belong in `raw/`; a verification payload or a note filed there is reported as set aside and left in place, but it still costs a step. On `INCOMPLETE`, `BLOCKED` or `NEEDS_CONTEXT` (never accepted as a finished scope), and on a `DONE` that left slices open, `keryx review retry-plan --manifest <package>/slices/manifest.json --result <package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt --package <package>` decides and hands out the next wave of only the slices still uncovered (`--next-wave` plans one without a result). A result that covered a new slice spends no attempt; two results in a row with nothing new, or six failed rounds, print the `- **Not run:** …` line to paste into the report, and a result with nothing new first has its open slices cut in half. `keryx review slice --package <package>` already wrote one driver per reviewer x wave (`drivers/<reviewer>-w<n>.json`: slice ids, absolute slice paths, `result` path; the dispatcher adds `model`). Dispatch each wave in one batch, save each reply to its driver's `result`, and after each batch run `keryx review next --package <package>` (never `retry-plan` once per reviewer): it returns every reviewer's next wave at once, with reason `missing`, `retry`, `stalled` or `escalated`, or `done`. After a crash or timeout run it first: it collects late results from `<package>/raw/` and never re-hands a finished slice. Only the operator can accept a smaller set than that (`review_override_reviewers`, or `keryx review override-reviewers` in their terminal). An unfinished reviewer is never counted as a clean pass. **Persist every result, on every host.** On keryx shell pass each reviewer `save_result_to: <package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt`: the host writes its full final text there. Elsewhere the prompt tells the reviewer to write its whole reply to `<package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt` before it answers. Either way `review complete` has raw evidence after the transcript is cut, and you parse that file, never the tool output. Build `research.json` with `keryx review ledger build --package <package>` — never by hand: it reads the saved results, `scope-files.json` and the retry state, marks a reviewer complete only when its result is finished and its payloads cover the scope, and prints each gap with the exact next command and the waves left (a `retry-plan --next-wave` call, or a `--dispositions` entry for a raw finding). Run `keryx review ingest --research <package>/research.json` once it prints READY (exit 0). A refused `review complete` names what is missing: fix that with a command and run it again; it is never `blocked`. `--head` wants a SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`), not `HEAD`.
 5. **Never print a scope or a slice.** The tool output of one call is cut at about 20 KB and `keryx review scope` of a large PR prints hundreds of KB. Run it as `keryx review scope --ref <base> --json > .metaproject/data/review/scope.json` and read the counts from the file (`keryx ctx read`, or `jq`); take `<base>` from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, not a guessed `origin/main`. Create `.metaproject/data/review/` first (`mkdir -p`) — a missing directory is a command to run, not a blocker. **Machine artifacts by direct write.** Save slices, payloads and results by redirection or `keryx ctx run --raw -- <command>`; the summarized form of `keryx ctx run` drops the bytes a later step parses.
 6. **Write mutants whole.** A testing reviewer's `mutant_candidates` cover every changed branch, code downstream of the diff included. Write them to `research-evidence/mutants.json` unchanged; you may not narrow them, and a candidate no pass has run still blocks the coverage gate (`SKILL.detail.md`, mutation pass).
 7. **Measure before `review-layout`.** Run the browser measurements (Playwright/Storybook) yourself and pass them in its first dispatch (`context_files` on keryx shell, by path elsewhere); they count as evidence when the command and viewport are named. A second `NEEDS_CONTEXT` from one role is Not run (`layout: no engine`), not another refill (`SKILL.detail.md`).
 
 ## Control
 
 - **Profiles.** The default is read-only: one round, no edits. `--fix` hands the findings to `flow-orchestrator` or `task-implementer`; the orchestrator never edits code. Control returns to this main session after each hand-off, which loads this skill again (never the implementer, which would nest); each re-review counts toward the ceiling (it adds 1 to the count).
 - **Waves.** Split by diff domain (`core` = logic, security, architecture; `domain` = frontend, backend, conventions; `support` = style, tests), in that order; A/B/C/D below keep their dependency order, except Wave C, which starts early and overlaps A and B (see Wave C); Wave D runs after the last verifier pass. A full or `--all` round runs at most 10 reviewers per wave (`MAX_REVIEWERS_PER_WAVE_FULL`).
 - **Rate limits.** On a reviewer dispatch that fails with a rate-limit or overloaded error (reported as `STATUS: RATE_LIMITED`, a harness signal, not a schema status), halve the wave, requeue the rest and honour `retry-after`, at most 300 seconds (`MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS`). After at most two halvings (`MAX_RATE_HALVINGS`) stop with `STATUS: BLOCKED rate_limited`, naming the queue left.
 - **Early verdict.** When every reviewer and the verifier are done, save every verifier pass to `research-evidence/verifications.json`, then run `keryx review verdict <package>` (it reads `<package>/raw`; the shared `.metaproject/data/review/raw` only when passed as `--raw`, which mixes in other rounds) and give the operator the verdict then; refuted findings are excluded only once `verifications.json` exists, held ones only once Wave D's claims are saved to `research-evidence/premises.json`. A verdict given before Wave D ran is provisional, and you say so: it counts as open the findings the judge may still hold or lower. The mutation pass, ledger and `keryx review complete` continue as the tail, and every managed round finishes them. The verdict is interim: the round is not done until `complete` (`SKILL.detail.md` § "Early verdict").
 - **Recovery.** After a timeout or crash: collect, validate, ingest, then dispatch only what is missing with `keryx review next --package <package>` (all reviewers at once). Never re-dispatch a wave whose results are on disk; after a second timeout of the same reviewer change the task (fewer slices, narrower focus), not only the diff size (`SKILL.detail.md` § "Recovery").
-- **Done when** the consolidated report and the `keryx:findings` block are emitted and the stage counts and **Not run** are stated. A managed round (not `lightweight`, which is report-only) is also done only when every dispatched reviewer's result is recorded with `keryx review ingest` and `keryx review complete` has run. `completed` means `keryx review readiness` passed, or each failing item but `premise-decisions` (answered per finding, never waived) is waived by the operator: in keryx shell call `review_waive_readiness` (a card, never a terminal), then run `keryx review complete`; elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review complete <package> --waive <item> "<their words>"` in their terminal; unattended, record Not run; publishing to GitHub is held by the same checklist, and a not-ready package goes out only through `keryx review publish --partial` (in keryx shell: `review_publish` with `partial: true`).
+- **Done when** the consolidated report and the `keryx:findings` block are emitted and the stage counts and **Not run** are stated. A managed round (not `lightweight`, which is report-only) is also done only when every dispatched reviewer's result is recorded with `keryx review ingest` and the `review_complete` card has been answered (an agent never runs `keryx review complete`; that command is for a human in a terminal). `completed` means `keryx review readiness` passed, or each failing item but `premise-decisions` (answered per finding, never waived) is waived by the operator: in keryx shell call `review_waive_readiness` (a card, never a terminal), then call `review_complete`; elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review complete <package> --waive <item> "<their words>"` in their terminal; unattended, record Not run; publishing to GitHub is held by the same checklist, and a not-ready package goes out only through `keryx review publish --partial` (in keryx shell: `review_publish` with `partial: true`).
 
 ---
 
 ## Step 12 — the `keryx:findings` block
 
 The prose report is for a human. **`keryx review ingest` reads the fenced block,
 not the prose**, and a round that emits only prose cannot be used to build the
 next round's input — the reviewer's `confidence`, `evidence`, `impact` and
 `suggested_fix` do not survive rendering, and no regex recovers what was never
 written down.
 
 So every report ends with one fenced block whose info string carries
 `keryx:findings`:
 
 ````text
 ```json keryx:findings
 [ { …one object per finding, conforming to review-finding.schema.json… } ]
 ```
 ````

# Changelog
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
-### A project rule under `rules/project/core/` replaces its bundled twin
-
-- **Fixed:** `keryx skills resolve-context` treats a project rule at `.metaproject/rules/project/core/<name>.mdc` as replacing the bundled `.metaproject/rules/core/<name>.mdc`, as it already did for `rules/project/<name>.mdc`: the entry carries `shadows` (reason `replaces-bundled` when nothing else selects it) and the bundled rule is no longer listed. `keryx skills import` puts a cited rule that keryx also ships in that slot, so a worker used to get both conflicting files as `must_read`, and a project copy whose globs matched nothing was left out entirely.
-
-### A citation with a heading anchor cites its document
-
-- **Fixed:** a backticked citation that carries a heading anchor, such as `` `docs/x.md#some-heading` `` or `` `core/x.mdc#part` ``, now counts as a citation of the file. `keryx skills resolve-context` lists it as a `referenced-by` contract, and `keryx skills references check` / `suggest` see it, so a declared document cited only by `path#anchor` is no longer reported as `unused-declaration`.

 ## [0.3.123] - 2026-10-18
 
 ### Conditional mandatory reads for documents cited by project rules (flow 462, PR #1048)
 
 - **Added:** `.metaproject/rules/project/references.json` (schema 1) declares, per cited document, a path, `when.globs` and `when.keywords`, an anchor and a description. A second declaration of one normalised path is refused; a malformed file warns and turns promotion off, it never blocks.
 - **Added:** `keryx skills resolve-context --task-text '<text>'` (text beyond 4000 characters is truncated with a warning) promotes a declared reference from `on_demand` to `must_read` when a glob matches a touched path or a keyword occurs in the task text (keywords starting with `.` or `@` match). The entry carries its reason: `condition:glob:<g>`, `condition:keyword:<k>` or `declared`. Promoted entries are never dropped by the byte cap. A dead anchor falls back to the whole file with a warning.
 - **Added:** proof of reading is checked by `contracts validate`: path, sha256 pin and drift, an anchor equal to the declared one, and a summary of at least 40 characters that shares at least three distinct words of five or more letters with the anchored section (fewer when the section has fewer). `how: n/a` counts as a miss. The check is a vocabulary proxy, not proof of understanding.
 - **Added:** `keryx skills references check [--json]` (declarations, anchors, citations, linked imports scanned at their origin with a size cap) and `keryx skills references suggest` (writes no file).
 - **Added:** TUI: sidebar `refs p/n`, a References tab, `/projectctx refs`, states R0–R7; polling does not overlap a load still in flight; reference text is sanitised before it is rendered.
 - **Changed:** the flow-orchestrator, task-implementer, tests-creator, job-orchestrator and orchestrator-prompt skills pass `--task-text` single-quoted with `'` written as `'\''`; docs, README and a live-run runbook (`docs/requirements/keryx-conditional-reads/live-run.md`) updated; `docs:check` script added.
 - **Changed:** `last.json` of the resolver records only `taskTextLength` and `taskTextTruncated`, never the task text (acceptance criterion AC3 amended).
 
 ### Shell startup, recovery and source scanning (PR #1035)
 
 - **Added:** opt-in JSONL diagnostics via `KERYX_SHELL_STARTUP_TRACE`: startup stages and event-loop timer lateness. See [Diagnose shell startup](docs/docs/guides/shell-startup.md).
 - **Changed:** orientation reuses one Git status result per preparation and removes an unused branch probe. No cross-preparation cache; failed checks remain unknown. No fixed speedup or complete animation-stall fix is guaranteed.
 - **Fixed:** interactive OpenAI recovery allows at most three retries per pending model round for HTTP 403 with the exact message `Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later.`, using cancellable backoff. Other transient errors do not reset the counter. Ordinary authorization failures do not qualify; non-interactive behavior is unchanged.
 - **Fixed:** filesystem JavaScript/TypeScript scans use optional parser context to distinguish `.env` property access from private-file references. Missing context or invalid syntax retains conservative findings with a warning; ambiguous matches remain. Output checks and secret redaction are unchanged. Misleading key/address examples were removed from shell UI source.
 
 ## [0.3.122] - 2026-10-17

# TM-04: Operator Confirmation Cards
 
 ## Decisions Only the Operator May Take, Asked as a Card in `keryx shell`, and What a Card Does Not Prove
 
 **Status**: Implemented
 **Frozen**: 2026-10-15
 **Task**: flow 456
 **Depends on**: TM-03 (terminal confirmation token). This record changes where the operator answers, not what the answer is worth. Flow 295 (`schedule_create`) is the pattern it generalises.
 **Reviewer Track**: architecture
 
 ---
 
 ## 1. Purpose
 
-Thirteen keryx decisions are the operator's alone: lifting a review pass ceiling, posting a review to GitHub, waiving unreviewed files or a readiness item, minting a flow completion token, landing an external agent's patch, accepting, promoting or graduating a learned pattern, and changing or running a schedule. Each CLI path refuses unless stdin and stdout are terminals. Inside `keryx shell` the agent runs commands through `shell_exec`, which has no terminal, so it stopped and told the operator to open another terminal and type a long command.
+Nineteen keryx decisions are the operator's alone: lifting a review pass ceiling, confirming a review plan, deciding a held finding's premise, closing a review round, posting a review to GitHub, waiving unreviewed files or a readiness item, minting a flow completion token, landing an external agent's patch, accepting, promoting or graduating a learned pattern, and changing or running a schedule. Each CLI path refuses unless stdin and stdout are terminals. Inside `keryx shell` the agent runs commands through `shell_exec`, which has no terminal, so it stopped and told the operator to open another terminal and type a long command.
 
 This record replaces that hand-off. In `keryx shell` each decision is a native tool. The tool shows the operator a card (what is decided, the exact effect, the subject) and takes a yes or no. The terminal paths stay exactly as they were.
 
 ## 2. The tools
 
 | Tool | Same effect as |
 |---|---|
 | `review_chunks_answer` | `keryx review chunks estimate --answer yes\|no` |
+| `review_confirm_plan` | `keryx review confirm-plan` |
+| `review_decide_premise` | `keryx review decide-premise` |
+| `review_complete` | `keryx review complete` (closes the round after every gate passes; the head is the recorded manifest head, not one the model supplies. The agent completes a review only through this card; the CLI stays for a human in a terminal) |
 | `review_publish` | `keryx review publish` |
 | `review_waive_coverage` | `keryx review complete --waive-coverage` (records the waiver only) |
 | `review_waive_readiness` | `keryx review complete --waive <item>` (records the waiver only) |
 | `flow_confirm` | `keryx flow confirm <id> [--merged]` |
 | `external_apply` | `keryx agents external apply <run-id>` |
 | `learn_accept`, `learn_promote`, `learn_graduate` | `keryx learn accept`, `promote`, `graduate apply` |

 The framework is `src/commands/operator-confirm-tools.ts`. The specs are in `operator-confirm-review.ts` and `operator-confirm-other.ts`.
 
 **How a call runs.**
 1. `buildCard` reads the real state on disk and builds the card. A card is never built from the model's input alone. A refusal (nothing to confirm) ends the call without asking.
 2. The tool declares a confirmation, so the approval gate treats it as a hard floor: every permission mode asks (`auto` included), review-auto never grants it, no saved pattern or MCP trust grant applies, and an unattended run is denied.
 3. The card's single-use token lives in the shell process's memory. It reaches `invoke` only after the operator's yes. A declined or denied card drops it; a replay finds nothing.
 4. On yes, `apply` calls the same library function the CLI calls, in process, and re-checks that the state did not move between the card and the yes.
 5. The decision is stored with `confirmedVia`: `tui-card` when the operator answered in this shell, `remote-card` when they answered in the session's remote topic. The quote is the card title plus `: yes`.
 
 ## 3. What a card proves
 
 A person pressed yes, in this keryx shell session or in its remote topic, on a card whose text was built from the state that the decision then changed. For the remote topic, "a person" means an account on the remote allowlist (`src/remote/config.ts`) answering in the session's own topic, the same rule that governs every other remote approval. A card is never weaker than an existing `alwaysAsk` approval.

## 5. Why child-process proofs were rejected
 
 The first idea was to let the CLI accept an environment variable, a file or a socket that proves "the shell's operator said yes", so the existing commands could stay the only implementation. It was rejected. `shell_exec` runs whatever command line the model writes, in an environment the model controls (`sh -c`), as a user who can read and write everything the operator can. Anything handed to that child can be read, copied or replayed by the model, so the proof would prove only that the model ran the command.
 
 The in-process tool has no such surface. The decision never leaves the shell process: no argument, environment variable, file or socket carries it. `ask_user` was rejected for a different reason: it can be answered by review-auto, the arbiter or an answers file, and its answer returns through the model.
 
 ## 6. Remote answering
 
 A card raised while the remote topic is active is mirrored to the topic like any other approval. The first answer wins: a press in the topic closes the dock, an answer in the dock removes the buttons in the topic. When the topic answers, the gate records `confirmedVia: "remote-card"`, so a record always says where the yes came from. Silence in the topic never ends the dock.
 
 ### 6a. What a Telegram answer proves, and what it does not
 
 Flow 464 puts the four review acts that used to need a terminal (`review confirm-plan`, `review decide-premise`, `review complete --waive` and `--waive-coverage`, `review complete`) behind cards: `review_confirm_plan`, `review_decide_premise`, `review_waive_readiness` / `review_waive_coverage`, and `review_complete`. A card the topic answers is accepted only when all of these hold: the press comes from a Telegram user id in the binding's `allowedUserIds` (a binding with none refuses every remote answer), it carries this question's token, the token is unused, and it is under one hour old. Each refusal leaves the token spent. The record keeps `pressedBy` (the Telegram user id) and `pressedAt` (the shell's clock, not Telegram's) beside `confirmedVia: "remote-card"`. A card answered in the shell has neither field. If the topic cannot be reached, the card says "Telegram mirror not delivered" and is answered in the shell.
 
 What the press proves: someone logged in to an allowed Telegram account pressed yes on this card, within the hour, once.
 
 What it does not prove:
 
 - **That a person pressed.** An agent running as the same OS user can write the stores the shell reads (the confirmation records, the review package JSON) without any card, exactly the limit TM-03 and §4 state. A card narrows the honest path; it does not stop that agent.
-- **That the bot token is out of the agent's reach.** The token that posts and reads the topic sits in the shell's environment or config, which an agent in the same session can read. Holding it, the agent can post as the bot and read updates. It cannot make Telegram report a press from an allowed user id, but it can talk to the bot API, so a press is evidence of an allowed account, not of an unreachable channel.
+- **That the bot token is out of the agent's reach.** The token that posts and reads the topic sits in the shell's environment or in the `BOT_TOKEN_FILE` file (owner-only, but readable by an agent running as the same OS user). Holding it, the agent can post as the bot and read updates. It cannot make Telegram report a press from an allowed user id, but it can talk to the bot API, so a press is evidence of an allowed account, not of an unreachable channel.
+- **That the operator read the text the shell holds.** Whoever holds the bot token can edit or replace the text of the mirrored card. A press proves a press on a card with the real approval id, not that the operator read what the shell built.
+- **That a card survives a restart.** The token and the TUI card view are process memory. A restart drops every pending card; a later press is refused with no record, and the operator asks again. A late press is also refused by serve's expiry or its resolved state, not only by keryx's token rules.
 - **Message order.** Telegram can drop, delay or reorder messages. A dropped card leaves the shell waiting (the dock stays open); a delayed press can arrive after the question was answered or has aged out, and is refused by the token rules above. Nothing in the answer proves the operator saw the card text last shown, only that this token was pressed.
 
 The pending cards (age and time left of the token) and the answered ones (with `pressedBy`) are shown in the `/remote-control` status tab, the sidebar Remote row and the `/decisions` modal.
 
 ## 7. Unattended runs
 
 An unattended run has no approver, so the answer to a card is no. `src/trigger/unattended.ts` also lists every card tool as interactive-only and refuses it by name. The skills that used to say "ask the operator to run this in a terminal" now say: in `keryx shell` call the tool and let the operator answer it; never send the operator to a terminal; when the run is unattended, record the item as Not run, as before.

 ## Fix rounds — dispositions, regressions, withdrawal
 
 ### Every prior finding leaves the round with a disposition
 
 A fix round that reports only new findings is unreadable: the author cannot tell
 which of their fixes landed. Close the loop explicitly — one line per prior
 finding, in the report, before the new findings:
 
 | Disposition | Meaning |
 |---|---|
 | `closed` | Checked against the code, not against the commit message, and the defect is gone |
 | `open` | The fix does not reach the defect; say what is still true |
 | `partial` | One site of the class was fixed and the enumeration named others |
 | `regressed` | The fix removed this defect and introduced another — file the new one separately |
 | `withdrawn` | The finding was wrong. See below |
 
 **Check the code, not the commit message.** A commit titled *"report an abandoned
 sync as abandoned"* is a claim; the disposition is whether the branch it renamed
 is reachable and pinned. On a recorded round, two such commits asserted behaviour

## Slices, waves and results — every host; keryx shell specifics marked
 
 A reviewer starts in the project root and reads project files; a path outside the project root is unreadable to it. On keryx shell its `context_files` content reaches it wrapped as DATA, and slices and measurements travel only there (never pasted or retyped); elsewhere the prompt names the slice paths. `skill_path` and `pr_context` stay payload fields. The text reaches the reviewer in slices small enough to finish.
 
 0. **Publish the plan before anything else (keryx shell).** Your first tool call is `plan_set` with `step-0`…`step-14` and `step-10b` all `pending`. A shell turn that has open plan items is continued by the host; a turn that ends on a text reply is over, and a message saying the review "cannot be honestly completed" ends the run with nothing reviewed. Never end the turn while a step is `pending` or `in_progress`: mark it `blocked` only with a cause you cannot fix with a command, and otherwise keep working. Step 6a then updates this plan rather than creating it.
 1. **Slice first.** `keryx review slice --ref <base> --package <package> --host <host>` after `keryx review start`. It writes `<package>/slices/slice-NN.diff` files of at most 150000 bytes each and a `manifest.json` carrying a wave budget (`--wave-bytes`, never below the slice ceiling; default by `--host`: 60000 on keryx-shell, 150000 elsewhere): what ONE reviewer dispatch may total, so a role owning many slices is dispatched in slice waves that each fit the child deadline. On keryx shell with a large diff pass a small `--max-bytes` (for example 18000) and `--wave-bytes` (for example 54000) so no wave outruns a reviewer's five minutes; ledgers (csv, lockfiles, snapshots, generated files) are listed under `omissions` with a reason — list them in the report as not reviewed, never as clean.
 2. **Slices travel by path; on keryx shell, only by `context_files`.** The slices sit under the project (`<package>/slices`). On keryx shell pass each reviewer its slice paths in `spawn_subagent`'s `context_files`: the host copies the text into that reviewer's task, so you never paste or retype a slice. Elsewhere name the slice paths in the prompt. Put the `slices` ids in its reviewer-input. A dispatch that names a git range but no slice leaves the reviewer with nothing to read — that is `BLOCKED`, not a review.
 3. **Check before dispatch, every payload.** `keryx review dispatch-check --payload <file> --manifest <package>/slices/manifest.json --package <package>` for the wave; exit 1 means a payload names no slice, is over the wave ceiling (dispatch fewer slices, then the next wave), names a `skill_path` or `context_doc` that does not exist (`REVIEWER_INPUT_PATH_MISSING`), belongs to an unconfirmed over-threshold plan (`REVIEWER_INPUT_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED`), or breaks `reviewer-input.schema.json`. Fix it; do not dispatch around it.
 4. **One batch.** Dispatch the whole wave — up to 10 reviewers — in one message, not one at a time. On keryx shell every round reviewer's `spawn_subagent` carries `review_wave: {"package": "<package>", "pass": "round"}` (a wave outside it counts against the turn's 32 children) and a `timeout_ms` that fits its wave: the default 300000 is sized for a wave of 60000 bytes, so a larger `--wave-bytes` needs a larger `timeout_ms`. Give each reviewer `max_rounds` of at least 40 (the default); a reviewer that spends its rounds reading the skill and the schema returns nothing. **Incomplete means the next wave while it makes progress, Not run when it stalls.** Every reviewer result lists the `slices` it covered, in its `REVIEW_RESULT` object, as ids (`"slices": ["slice-01", "slice-02"]`); an object with an `id` and an optional `coverage` note (`{"id": "slice-01", "coverage": "read in full"}`) is read the same way. An object with a `status` counts only when it is DONE, COMPLETE, COVERED or OK (any case); a slice marked NOT_READ, INCOMPLETE, SKIPPED or PARTIAL is not covered, so give a slice you did not read no `status` of that kind and leave it out. An entry with no id counts for nothing. **One driver file per dispatch.** Write `<package>/drivers/<reviewer>.json` with `{"reviewer": "<name>", "slices": [<ids dispatched>], "result": "raw/<reviewer>.txt", "definition": "<path of the reviewer's SKILL.md>"}`: `ledger build` takes the reviewer's rule file from `definition` (a `skill_path` there, or inside a `payload` object, is read too) and the slices it was handed from `slices`. Only reviewer replies belong in `raw/`; a verification payload or a note filed there is reported as set aside and left in place, but it still costs a step. On `INCOMPLETE`, `BLOCKED` or `NEEDS_CONTEXT` (never accepted as a finished scope), and on a `DONE` that left slices open, `keryx review retry-plan --manifest <package>/slices/manifest.json --result <package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt --package <package>` decides and hands out the next wave of only the slices still uncovered (`--next-wave` plans one without a result). A result that covered a new slice spends no attempt; two results in a row with nothing new, or six failed rounds, print the `- **Not run:** …` line to paste into the report, and a result with nothing new first has its open slices cut in half. `keryx review slice --package <package>` already wrote one driver per reviewer x wave (`drivers/<reviewer>-w<n>.json`: slice ids, absolute slice paths, `result` path; the dispatcher adds `model`). Dispatch each wave in one batch, save each reply to its driver's `result`, and after each batch run `keryx review next --package <package>` (never `retry-plan` once per reviewer): it returns every reviewer's next wave at once, with reason `missing`, `retry`, `stalled` or `escalated`, or `done`. After a crash or timeout run it first: it collects late results from `<package>/raw/` and never re-hands a finished slice. Only the operator can accept a smaller set than that (`review_override_reviewers`, or `keryx review override-reviewers` in their terminal). An unfinished reviewer is never counted as a clean pass. **Persist every result, on every host.** On keryx shell pass each reviewer `save_result_to: <package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt`: the host writes its full final text there. Elsewhere the prompt tells the reviewer to write its whole reply to `<package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt` before it answers. Either way `review complete` has raw evidence after the transcript is cut, and you parse that file, never the tool output. Build `research.json` with `keryx review ledger build --package <package>` — never by hand: it reads the saved results, `scope-files.json` and the retry state, marks a reviewer complete only when its result is finished and its payloads cover the scope, and prints each gap with the exact next command and the waves left (a `retry-plan --next-wave` call, or a `--dispositions` entry for a raw finding). Run `keryx review ingest --research <package>/research.json` once it prints READY (exit 0). A refused `review complete` names what is missing: fix that with a command and run it again; it is never `blocked`. `--head` wants a SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`), not `HEAD`.
 5. **Never print a scope or a slice.** The tool output of one call is cut at about 20 KB and `keryx review scope` of a large PR prints hundreds of KB. Run it as `keryx review scope --ref <base> --json > .metaproject/data/review/scope.json` and read the counts from the file (`keryx ctx read`, or `jq`); take `<base>` from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, not a guessed `origin/main`. Create `.metaproject/data/review/` first (`mkdir -p`) — a missing directory is a command to run, not a blocker. **Machine artifacts by direct write.** Save slices, payloads and results by redirection or `keryx ctx run --raw -- <command>`; the summarized form of `keryx ctx run` drops the bytes a later step parses.
 6. **Write mutants whole.** A testing reviewer's `mutant_candidates` cover every changed branch, code downstream of the diff included. Write them to `research-evidence/mutants.json` unchanged; you may not narrow them, and a candidate no pass has run still blocks the coverage gate (`SKILL.detail.md`, mutation pass).
 7. **Measure before `review-layout`.** Run the browser measurements (Playwright/Storybook) yourself and pass them in its first dispatch (`context_files` on keryx shell, by path elsewhere); they count as evidence when the command and viewport are named. A second `NEEDS_CONTEXT` from one role is Not run (`layout: no engine`), not another refill (`SKILL.detail.md`).
 
 ## Control
 
 - **Profiles.** The default is read-only: one round, no edits. `--fix` hands the findings to `flow-orchestrator` or `task-implementer`; the orchestrator never edits code. Control returns to this main session after each hand-off, which loads this skill again (never the implementer, which would nest); each re-review counts toward the ceiling (it adds 1 to the count).
 - **Waves.** Split by diff domain (`core` = logic, security, architecture; `domain` = frontend, backend, conventions; `support` = style, tests), in that order; A/B/C/D below keep their dependency order, except Wave C, which starts early and overlaps A and B (see Wave C); Wave D runs after the last verifier pass. A full or `--all` round runs at most 10 reviewers per wave (`MAX_REVIEWERS_PER_WAVE_FULL`).
 - **Rate limits.** On a reviewer dispatch that fails with a rate-limit or overloaded error (reported as `STATUS: RATE_LIMITED`, a harness signal, not a schema status), halve the wave, requeue the rest and honour `retry-after`, at most 300 seconds (`MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS`). After at most two halvings (`MAX_RATE_HALVINGS`) stop with `STATUS: BLOCKED rate_limited`, naming the queue left.
 - **Early verdict.** When every reviewer and the verifier are done, save every verifier pass to `research-evidence/verifications.json`, then run `keryx review verdict <package>` (it reads `<package>/raw`; the shared `.metaproject/data/review/raw` only when passed as `--raw`, which mixes in other rounds) and give the operator the verdict then; refuted findings are excluded only once `verifications.json` exists, held ones only once Wave D's claims are saved to `research-evidence/premises.json`. A verdict given before Wave D ran is provisional, and you say so: it counts as open the findings the judge may still hold or lower. The mutation pass, ledger and `keryx review complete` continue as the tail, and every managed round finishes them. The verdict is interim: the round is not done until `complete` (`SKILL.detail.md` § "Early verdict").
 - **Recovery.** After a timeout or crash: collect, validate, ingest, then dispatch only what is missing with `keryx review next --package <package>` (all reviewers at once). Never re-dispatch a wave whose results are on disk; after a second timeout of the same reviewer change the task (fewer slices, narrower focus), not only the diff size (`SKILL.detail.md` § "Recovery").
-- **Done when** the consolidated report and the `keryx:findings` block are emitted and the stage counts and **Not run** are stated. A managed round (not `lightweight`, which is report-only) is also done only when every dispatched reviewer's result is recorded with `keryx review ingest` and `keryx review complete` has run. `completed` means `keryx review readiness` passed, or each failing item but `premise-decisions` (answered per finding, never waived) is waived by the operator: in keryx shell call `review_waive_readiness` (a card, never a terminal), then run `keryx review complete`; elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review complete <package> --waive <item> "<their words>"` in their terminal; unattended, record Not run; publishing to GitHub is held by the same checklist, and a not-ready package goes out only through `keryx review publish --partial` (in keryx shell: `review_publish` with `partial: true`).

 ## Step 12 — the `keryx:findings` block
 
 The prose report is for a human. **`keryx review ingest` reads the fenced block,
 not the prose**, and a round that emits only prose cannot be used to build the
 next round's input — the reviewer's `confidence`, `evidence`, `impact` and
 `suggested_fix` do not survive rendering, and no regex recovers what was never
 written down.
 
 So every report ends with one fenced block whose info string carries
 `keryx:findings`:
 
 ````text
 ```json keryx:findings
 [ { …one object per finding, conforming to review-finding.schema.json… } ]
 ```
 ````
